articles.title: Big blow for New Zealand! Star batter ruled out of remainder of ODI series against India
articles.summary: New Zealand have suffered a setback ahead of the second ODI against India, with opener Devon Conway ruled out of the remaining matches of the five-game
articles.body: New Zealand have suffered a setback ahead of the second ODI against India, with opener Devon Conway ruled out of the remaining matches of the five-game series after sustaining a concussion during a training session on Tuesday.Conway suffered the injury while fielding during practice, forcing him out of the remainder of the ODI series. Left-handed batter Nick Kelly, who was initially selected for the fourth and fifth ODIs, will now join the squad in Wellington on Friday as his replacement.There was some relief for the New Zealand camp, however, as Matt Henry, who was involved in the fielding mishap that resulted in Conway's injury, has been cleared of concussion.The development comes after New Zealand lost the opening ODI to India in Auckland on Wednesday. Virat Kohli's authoritative 74, coupled with impressive bowling performances from Arshdeep Singh and Anshul Kamboj, helped India secure a comfortable victory in the rain-affected contest.Arshdeep led the attack with four wickets, while Gurnoor Brar picked up three scalps and Kamboj claimed two as New Zealand were bowled out for 185. India then chased down the revised target of 143 in 32 overs despite rain interruptions.The second ODI will be played at Sky Stadium in Wellington on Saturday, with New Zealand looking to bounce back and level the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs New Zealand: Rain keeps India indoors in Wellington; Siraj selection adds to intrigue
articles.summary: Wellington: Steady drizzle in Wellington on Friday forced New Zealand to shift their training to an indoor facility opposite the Basin Reserve, while
articles.body: Wellington: Steady drizzle in Wellington on Friday forced New Zealand to shift their training to an indoor facility opposite the Basin Reserve, while India cancelled their training session and stayed back at their hotel on the eve of the second ODI of the five-match series on Saturday.The turnaround time between the Auckland and Wellington fixtures permitted only one practice session for both teams following their travel day on November 5. While players who were part of India's T20I set-up have already had a taste of the windy Welly, most will walk straight into action, hoping to acclimatise quickly. New Zealand poses stiff challenges, and the varying ground dimensions and weather conditions across the country present different hurdles to overcome.From the short straight at Eden Park to the shorter square at Hnry Stadium, even the bowlers from both teams will need to make that quick adjustment because what worked in Auckland may or may not reap rewards in Wellington. For Kiwi quick Blair Tickner, it's about getting the work done in whatever time you get and finding the right balance between fixtures."We still do a bit of bowling between. You can't do it every time, there's guys going in and out of the session and we're just balancing that, and a lot of guys going to Test cricket as well, so there's a lot of balance happening. We have a great team and they are all sort of scheduling each bowler where they need to be, so now it's working so far, so good," said Tickner on the cramped schedule."I'm still coming back from a few injuries in the winter, so I'm sort of trying to bowl a bit more. I love bowling, getting that rhythm right, so I'm definitely still bowling in training and getting me to it," added the fast bowler, who flexed his muscles by smashing four massive sixes in Auckland.Tickner enjoyed putting on a show for the crowd but now wants to put up an improved performance with the ball at a venue where Abhishek Sharma blew the hosts away with a 38-ball 113. With lessons learnt, New Zealand will continue to come hard at India, and attack will be the mantra for the hosts."If the perfect plan works out, we are going to be attacking and get early wickets. That's the dream, and every one day team's bowling attack wants to bowl teams out, so we're looking to bowl teams out first before thinking about defensive play. We'll work it out there," said Tickner.Siraj has joined the team and is available for selection, but the management will take a call, whether he will play or not.Mohammed Siraj or Auqib Nabi?India will have to decide whether to bench Nabi to make way for Siraj, who joined the team after finishing his India A duties. The experienced fast bowler linked up with the squad in Wellington and remains available for selection. A practice session could have offered hints about the team management's thinking, but fielding coach Subhadeep Ghosh kept his selection cards close to his chest."Siraj has joined the team and is available for selection, but the management will take a call whether he will play or not," said Ghosh.Given the weather conditions, it looks increasingly difficult for India to alter their bowling combination, and the only toss-up could be between Siraj and Nabi.There is a strong forecast of rain on match day as well, and the fans could be in for another frustrating day of cricket when the two teams take the field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aussies turn to 'Mr Cricket': Former CSK coach joins Australia support staff for Ashes and 2027 World Cup
articles.summary: Mike Hussey was on Friday appointed as a consultant coach to the Australian team for next year's Ashes series against England and the 2027 ODI World Cup.
articles.body: Mike Hussey was on Friday appointed as a consultant coach to the Australian team for next year's Ashes series against England and the 2027 ODI World Cup.The former Australia batter had revealed in August that England's new red-ball coach, Stephen Fleming, had informally approached him to take up the role of Test batting mentor. However, the 51-year-old turned down the offer and has instead decided to work with Australia as they look to address their batting struggles, which were exposed during their recent 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa.Hussey, who earned the nickname 'Mr Cricket' for his technical knowledge of the game, will also assist the Australian coaching staff during this month's home T20 series against England and the subsequent four-Test series against New Zealand.His role will extend beyond next year's assignments, with Hussey also set to work with Australia at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where cricket will feature, and the 2028 T20 World Cup."I am extremely excited about being a part of the team in a more formal and meaningful role in the coming years," said Hussey, who represented Australia in more than 300 international matches across all formats."This team has achieved so much in recent times, to which I hope I can add value to the coaching and playing groups ahead of what will be an exciting and challenging period."Hussey has considerable coaching experience, having worked with both Australia and England. He was part of England's coaching setup when they won the T20 World Cup in 2022 and served as Chennai Super Kings' long-time batting coach under Fleming in the Indian Premier League. He also coached Welsh Fire in this year's edition of The Hundred."Mike has been a highly valued part of our staff in the past and brings a considerable skill set which is complementary to the coaches and players," said Australia head coach Andrew McDonald."Not only is his expertise as a player and coach across multiple formats, competitions, countries invaluable, so are his qualities as a person."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Too early for him’: Sachin Tendulkar's blunt verdict on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s leadership role at 15
articles.summary: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already achieved milestones that remain a distant dream for many cricketers throughout their careers.
articles.body: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already achieved milestones that remain a distant dream for many cricketers throughout their careers. From finishing as the leading run-scorer in an Indian Premier League (IPL) season to smashing a match-winning century in the U-19 World Cup final to clinch the title, the teenager has made remarkable strides in a short span of time.However, his elevation to the role of East Zone vice-captain for the Duleep Trophy did not go down well with everyone. Among those who believe the youngster was handed a leadership responsibility too early is batting legend Sachin Tendulkar.Although Tendulkar had not publicly questioned the selectors' decision at the time of the announcement, he shared his reservations during a Reddit Q&A session, suggesting that Sooryavanshi should focus on gaining more experience in red-ball cricket before taking on such responsibilities.Responding to a fan who asked for his views on the 15-year-old being entrusted with a leadership role, Tendulkar said: "I feel it's too early for him to become a vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy. We have to let him play more matches with the red ball and take one step at a time!"Sooryavanshi had featured in just eight red-ball matches for Bihar before being named East Zone skipper Ishan Kishan's deputy. The decision meant he was preferred over Abhimanyu Easwaran, an experienced campaigner with more than 100 First-Class appearances.The East Zone selection committee subsequently clarified that the appointment was made with the youngster's development in mind and should not be interpreted as an indication of the pecking order within the squad.Sooryavanshi also got a taste of captaincy during the tournament when Kishan was forced to leave the field due to an injury. The teenager stepped in to lead the side and was involved in several important on-field decisions, including DRS calls. Videos of his involvement in those reviews also gained traction on social media.Meanwhile, Sooryavanshi has continued to strengthen his position in India's T20I setup, although he is yet to establish himself as a regular opener. The youngster faces competition for a place in the top three from established names such as Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan.Tendulkar names favourite captainsDuring the same interaction, Tendulkar also reflected on his own stint as India's captain, describing the opportunity to lead the national side as a tremendous honour. However, he admitted that the position did not always give him complete control over team selection.Tendulkar, who made his international debut on November 15, 1989, before bringing the curtain down on his career on November 16, 2013, also spoke about the changes in the functioning of Indian cricket over the years."It was a great honour to lead the team as captain. However, I didn’t always have the freedom to pick my team entirely on my own. The BCCI today is a far more professional organisation than it was in the 1990s. Indian cricket also went through a particularly dark phase during that period," Tendulkar said.Asked to name his favourite captains, the former India skipper singled out Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni, acknowledging the impact both had on Indian cricket."As far as my favourite captains go, Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni would definitely be at the top of my list!!," Tendulkar said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
